mainTopic: The trial of the מגדף, what counts as cursing ה׳'s name, and how the law applies to non-Jews, leading into the seven מצוות בני נח
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about the מגדף, someone who curses ה׳'s name. During the trial the עדים say 'Yosei' instead of the real curse. At the end, everyone else leaves, the oldest witness says the exact words, and the דיינים stand and tear their clothes. The גמרא then teaches that a מגדף is liable only if he curses the שם using the שם. שמואל learns this from the doubled 'נוקב שם' in the פסוק. The גמרא proves that נוקב means cursing, and rejects the readings 'making a hole' and 'pronouncing the name'. Next, a ברייתא teaches from 'איש איש' that non-Jews are also forbidden to curse ה׳, and they are punished by the sword. רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue about cursing with a כינוי, and רבי יצחק נפחא and רבי מיישא explain how this applies to a non-Jew. The amud ends by opening the list of the seven מצוות בני נח.

steps.title: During the trial, witnesses use a substitute name
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that each day of the trial, the עדים are questioned using a כינוי, such as 'Let Yosei strike Yosei,' instead of repeating the real curse.
steps.simpleTranslation: On each day of the trial, when the judges question the witnesses, the witnesses use a substitute name: 'Let Yosei strike Yosei.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains how the עדים testify during the trial without saying the actual curse against God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עדים must describe what the מגדף said, but repeating a curse on God's name would be terrible. So during questioning they swap in a stand-in name, 'Yosei.' This lets בית דין understand the case without the curse being said again.

keyTerms.meaning: The core teaching the גמרא will discuss
One who curses God's name (the subject of this משנה)
They question and examine the witnesses
A substitute name used in place of the real one
The stand-in name used instead of God's name

phrases.english: On every day [of the trial] they examine the witnesses
using a substitute name: "Let Yosei strike Yosei."
phrases.notes: Yosei (יוסי) has four letters, just like God's four-letter name, so it works as a stand-in.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכׇל יוֹם דָּנִין אֶת הָעֵדִים בְּכִינּוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's discussion of the מגדף from earlier in the daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the trial, the עדים testify using a כינוי ('Yosei') instead of the actual curse.

steps.title: For the final verdict, the oldest witness repeats the exact words in private
steps.stepSummary: At the end of the trial, בית דין does not execute based on testimony given with a כינוי. Everyone else is sent out, and the oldest witness is asked to say exactly what he heard.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the judgment is finished, they would not execute him based on the substitute name. Instead, they send everyone out. They ask the oldest of the witnesses and say to him: 'Say exactly what you heard.' And he says it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains that before sentencing, בית דין must hear the exact curse one time, from one witness, with no audience present.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Testimony using 'Yosei' was enough for the questioning, but it is not enough to put someone to death. בית דין must know for sure that the real שם was cursed. To keep this to a minimum, outsiders are removed and only the oldest witness says the words.

keyTerms.meaning: The judgment is finished (they are ready to rule)
The oldest (most senior) among the witnesses

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a death sentence needs exact, clear testimony, even when that testimony is painful to hear.

phrases.english: When the judgment is finished,
they would not execute [him] based on the substitute name,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording; some versions don't have it.

phrases.english: rather, they send everyone outside.
They ask the oldest among them [the witnesses]
and say to him: "Say exactly what you heard."
And he says it,

steps.triggerLanguage: נִגְמַר הַדִּין, לֹא הָיוּ הוֹרְגִין בְּכִינּוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a limit on step 1: the כינוי works for questioning but not for the death sentence
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before sentencing, outsiders are removed and the oldest witness repeats the exact curse.

steps.title: The judges stand and tear their clothes, never to mend them
steps.stepSummary: When the דיינים hear the actual curse, they stand up and tear their garments. They never fully sew the tear back together.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the judges stand on their feet and tear [their clothes], and they do not sew them back together.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes how the דיינים react when they hear the real curse: they stand and tear their clothes as a sign of mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hearing God's name cursed is treated like hearing terrible news, so the דיינים do קריעה. The tear is never properly sewn up, which shows how serious this is.

phrases.english: And the judges stand on their feet
and tear [their garments], and do not sew them back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes what the דיינים do right after the oldest witness repeats the curse
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The דיינים stand, tear their clothing, and never fully mend the tear.

steps.title: The other witnesses just say 'I heard the same'
steps.stepSummary: The second and third עדים do not repeat the curse. Each one simply says, 'I too heard like him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And the second witness says: 'I too heard like him.' And the third says: 'I too heard like him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends by saying the other witnesses confirm the testimony without saying the curse again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each witness still has to testify, but there is no need to repeat the curse. Saying 'I heard the same as him' counts as full testimony, so the curse is said only once.

keyTerms.meaning: The third (witness), if there is one

steps.whatToRemember: The full procedure: use 'Yosei' during questioning. At the end, send everyone out. The oldest witness says the exact words, and the דיינים stand and tear their clothes. The others just say 'I heard the same.'

phrases.english: And the second says: "I too [heard] like him,"
and the third says: "I too [heard] like him."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the testimony procedure that began with the oldest witness in step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The remaining עדים confirm by saying 'I too heard like him,' without repeating the curse.

steps.title: The מגדף is liable only if he cursed God's name with God's name
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא: the מגדף is not liable unless he 'blesses' (meaning curses) the שם using the שם.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: [He is not liable] unless he 'blesses' the Name with the Name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a ברייתא that defines exactly what kind of curse makes the מגדף liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's example, 'Let Yosei strike Yosei,' already hinted at a name striking a name. The ברייתא makes this a rule: the curse must use God's name against God's name. This sets up the גמרא's coming discussion of the definition.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Literally 'bless'; a polite way of saying 'curse'

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'יברך' does NOT mean bless. It is a polite word used so the text does not have to write 'curse' next to God's name.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught:
[He is not liable] unless he 'blesses' the Name with the Name.
phrases.notes: 'Blesses' is a polite way of saying 'curses.' It means something like 'Let Name strike Name,' like the Yosei example.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by defining the kind of curse the משנה is talking about
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מגדף is liable only when he curses God's name using God's name.

steps.title: What is the source for 'the שם with the שם'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the ברייתא's rule comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule it just quoted: a מגדף is only liable if he curses the שם using the שם. This question sets up שמואל's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave a rule without a source. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches that two mentions of the שם are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these words (learned)? A request for a source

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: He means the rule from the ברייתא we just saw: you are only liable for cursing the שם when you use the שם.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the scriptural source of the ברייתא in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches the requirement of שם בשם.

steps.title: שמואל's source: the פסוק says 'שם' twice
steps.stepSummary: שמואל points to ויקרא 24:16, which mentions נוקב שם twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: The פסוק says, 'One who curses the שם... when he curses the שם, he shall be put to death.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers that the source is the פסוק about the מגדף, which says 'נוקב שם' two times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have said it once. Saying 'שם' twice teaches that two names are involved: he curses the שם with the שם. So someone who curses the שם without using a name of הקב״ה is not liable for סקילה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who 'pierces' the שם, meaning one who curses it
He shall be put to death

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
As the verse states:
"And he who blasphemes the name, etc.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:16. The words וגו׳ mean the פסוק continues, and the גמרא skips to the part it needs.

phrases.english: when he blasphemes the name, he shall be put to death."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The doubled phrase נוקב שם / בנקבו שם in ויקרא 24:16 teaches שם בשם.

steps.title: How do we know נוקב means cursing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that the word נוקב refers to cursing.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that this word 'נוקב' is a term for cursing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now checks the meaning of the key word in שמואל's פסוק. It sets up a proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נוקב usually sounds like 'piercing.' Before using this פסוק as the source for the death penalty for cursing, the גמרא must show that נוקב can mean cursing.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do we know?
'Blessing', a polite way of saying cursing

steps.confusionAlert: In this סוגיא, 'ברכה' (blessing) about the שם always means cursing. The גמרא uses the opposite word so it does not have to say something terrible about הקב״ה.

phrases.english: From where do we know that this word "nokev"
is a term for blessing?
phrases.notes: 'Blessing' here really means cursing. It is a polite way of talking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the meaning of the key word in שמואל's source.

steps.title: Proof from בלעם, and the warning from אלהים לא תקלל
steps.stepSummary: בלעם used the word אקב to mean 'curse.' The אזהרה against cursing הקב״ה comes from אלהים לא תקלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'How shall I curse whom God has not cursed?' And the warning comes from here: 'You shall not curse God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that נוקב means cursing from בלעם's words, where קב means 'curse.' It also gives the separate warning (לאו) against this sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בלעם was hired to curse ישראל, so his 'אקב' must mean 'curse.' This shows the root נקב/קב can mean cursing. The punishment comes from ויקרא, but every punishment needs an אזהרה, and here it is אלהים לא תקלל.

keyTerms.meaning: A warning, the לאו that forbids an act that the תורה punishes

phrases.english: As it is written:
"How shall I curse whom God has not cursed?"
phrases.notes: במדבר 23:8. These are בלעם's words.

phrases.english: And its prohibition is from here:
"You shall not curse God."
phrases.notes: שמות 22:27.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 and adds the אזהרה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קב means curse, as in בלעם's words. The אזהרה is אלהים לא תקלל.

steps.title: Maybe נוקב means making a hole
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that נוקב might mean piercing, damaging a written שם, with a matching warning in דברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it means making a hole, as it is written: 'And he made a hole in its lid.' And the warning would come from here: 'And you shall destroy their name... You shall not do so to ה׳ your God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading of נוקב as cursing. It offers another meaning, making a hole, which would turn the פסוק into a ban on damaging a written שם of הקב״ה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word נקב clearly means 'hole' in מלכים. On this reading the death penalty would be for erasing or piercing a written שם, and that also has an אזהרה: לא תעשון כן. So the source for cursing is now in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: But say, a suggestion of another possibility
You shall not do so (the ban on destroying הקב״ה's name)

phrases.english: But say: it means making a hole,
as it is written: "And he made a hole in its lid,"
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 12:10.

phrases.english: and its prohibition would be from here:
"And you shall destroy their name...
phrases.notes: דברים 12:3–4. 'Their name' means the names of עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: You shall not do so to the Lord your God"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the meaning of נוקב that was proven in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that נוקב in ויקרא 24:16 means cursing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: נקב also means 'making a hole.' That reading has its own אזהרה, so the פסוק could be about damaging a written שם.

steps.title: The פסוק needs שם בשם, and that does not fit making a hole
steps.stepSummary: The meaning 'making a hole' does not work, because the פסוק requires שם בשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need 'the שם with the שם,' and that is not present.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the 'making a hole' reading. The doubled 'שם' in the פסוק requires the שם with the שם, and piercing cannot work that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל already showed that the פסוק demands two names: the שם acted upon using the שם. You can curse the שם by using the שם, but making a hole is not done 'with the שם.' So נוקב must mean cursing.
steps.whatToRemember: A מגדף is liable for סקילה only when he curses the שם using the שם. The source is the doubled נוקב שם in ויקרא, and נוקב means cursing (as in בלעם's words), not making a hole. The אזהרה is אלהים לא תקלל.
steps.whyThisMatters: The same requirement of שם בשם that defined the מגדף's sin is what rules out the other reading. This locks in both the source and the meaning of the word.

phrases.english: We require the name with the name,
phrases.notes: This comes from the doubled 'שם' in שמואל's פסוק.

phrases.english: and that is not present.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Uses the פסוק's own requirement (שם בשם) to rule out the other meaning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נוקב might mean making a hole in a written שם.
steps.terutzMaskana: Making a hole cannot be 'שם בשם', so נוקב means cursing.

steps.title: Placing two written names on top of each other and tearing them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a way to pierce a שם with a שם: stack two written names and tear through both at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe you could put two written names of God one on top of the other and tear through both together?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. It shows a way that 'piercing' could still involve a שם בשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said 'making a hole' cannot be the meaning, because the פסוק requires שם בשם. This challenge suggests a case where one name is physically on top of another and both are torn together. If that works, the 'piercing' reading comes back to life.

keyTerms.meaning: on each other, one on top of the other

phrases.english: But say that he places two names one on top of the other,
phrases.notes: He means two written names of הקב״ה, like on parchment.

phrases.english: and tears through them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 11 by finding a case of שם בשם that involves piercing.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 11 that piercing cannot fit the requirement of שם בשם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If two names are stacked and torn together, one name is pierced together with the other, so שם בשם seems possible after all.

steps.title: Stacked names are just two separate holes
steps.stepSummary: Tearing two stacked names is only making one hole and then another. It is not piercing one name by means of another.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is just making a hole, and then making another hole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that stacking does not create שם בשם. You have simply pierced two names, one after the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שם בשם means the name is the tool you use against the name. Here the tool is whatever is tearing, and each name just gets its own hole. So the case does not meet the requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: makes a hole and then makes a hole again

phrases.english: That is making a hole and then making a hole again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: it is two separate acts of piercing, not one name used on another.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Stacking two names and tearing them counts as piercing a name with a name.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is just two holes. Neither name is the tool, so there is no שם בשם.

steps.title: Engraving the name on a knife point and cutting with it
steps.stepSummary: A new attempt: engrave a שם on the tip of a knife and use that knife to cut through another written שם.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe he engraves a name of God on the point of a knife and cuts with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries again to find a real case of piercing a שם with a שם. This time the name sits on the cutting tool itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem in step 13 was that the name was not the tool. So now the name is put right on the tool's tip. That way the name seems to be what does the piercing.

keyTerms.meaning: the point or edge of a knife

phrases.english: But say that he engraves a name on the point of a knife,
and cuts with it?
phrases.notes: He cuts through another written name with that knife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 13 rejected stacking, this offers a new case where the name is on the tool.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that piercing can never be שם בשם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the name is on the cutting tip, the name itself seems to pierce the other name.

steps.title: The knife's sharpness does the cutting, not the name
steps.stepSummary: Even with a name on the knife, the sharp point is what cuts. The name has no role in the cutting.
steps.simpleTranslation: In that case, it is the sharp point of the knife that is cutting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the knife case. The cutting comes from the blade's sharpness, not from the engraved name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being physically on the tool does not make the name the cause of the hole. The sharp metal does the work. So piercing still never truly means 'name with name,' and the piercing reading stays rejected.
steps.whatToRemember: No physical case of piercing can be truly שם בשם, so נוקב cannot mean making a hole.

phrases.english: In that case, the sharp point of the knife
is what is cutting.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא חוּרְפָּא דְסַכִּינָא הוּא דְּקָא בָזַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the knife challenge and closes the piercing line.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the true cause of the act.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A name engraved on the knife makes the name the thing that pierces.
steps.terutzMaskana: The blade's sharpness pierces, not the name, so there is still no שם בשם.

steps.title: Maybe נוקב means pronouncing the explicit name
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that נוקב means pronouncing the שם המפורש. It brings a פסוק where נקבו means 'named,' and a warning from 'את ה׳ אלהיך תירא.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe נוקב means saying God's explicit name. We see this from 'which were pointed out (נקבו) by names.' The warning would come from 'You shall fear ה׳ your God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now offers a new meaning for נוקב: saying the name aloud, not cursing. It also supplies a matching warning for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, cursing came with a source for its meaning and a warning (אלהים לא תקלל). This challenge builds a full rival package. The meaning comes from נקבו בשמות in במדבר, and the warning comes from 'את ה׳ אלהיך תירא.'

keyTerms.meaning: were designated, pointed out by name

phrases.english: Say: it means pronouncing His explicit name,
as it is written: "And Moshe and Aharon took
these men
who were pointed out by names."
phrases.notes: במדבר 1:17. Here נקבו means 'said out by name,' so נוקב could mean saying the name.

phrases.english: And its warning comes from here:
"You shall fear ה׳ your God."
phrases.notes: דברים 6:13

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With piercing ruled out, the גמרא proposes a different alternative to cursing.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion in step 9 that נוקב means cursing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another פסוק uses the same root to mean 'name,' and there is a possible warning, so 'pronouncing the name' competes with 'cursing.'

steps.title: Two reasons pronouncing the name does not fit
steps.stepSummary: First, pronouncing the name has no שם בשם. Second, 'תירא' is a positive command, and a warning phrased as a positive command does not count as a real אזהרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: First, we need a name with a name, and that is missing. Also, the warning would be a positive command, and a positive command is not counted as a warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two separate answers that knock down the 'pronouncing the name' reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Answer one uses the same rule as step 11: the פסוק demands שם בשם, and just saying the name does not do that. Answer two attacks the warning. Punishment needs a לאו-type warning, and 'את ה׳ אלהיך תירא' is phrased as an עשה, so it cannot serve as the אזהרה.

keyTerms.meaning: a warning written as a positive command

steps.confusionAlert: 'את ה׳ אלהיך תירא' does imply that one must not act disrespectfully toward ה׳, but it is written as a positive command (do this), not as a לאו (don't do this). A warning written as a positive command does not count as an אזהרה for punishment.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that an אזהרת עשה is not an אזהרה comes up across ש״ס whenever the גמרא looks for the warning behind a punishment.

phrases.english: One reason: we need a name with a name,
and that is missing.
And also, it would be a warning stated as a positive command,
and a warning stated as a positive command is not considered a warning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16 with two independent reasons.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Double rejection: the requirement of the פסוק is missing, and the warning source is invalid.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נוקב could mean pronouncing the name, with 'תירא' as the warning.
steps.terutzMaskana: Pronouncing has no שם בשם, and an עשה cannot be an אזהרה, so cursing remains the meaning.

steps.title: Second proof: ויקב sits right next to ויקלל
steps.stepSummary: Another proof that נוקב means cursing: in the story of the מקלל, the פסוק says 'ויקב' and then 'ויקלל,' showing the two mean the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you prefer: the פסוק says 'he blasphemed... and cursed,' which shows that נוקב means cursing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, simpler proof that נוקב means cursing, taken straight from the מקלל story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of relying on בלעם's word אקב (step 9), the גמרא points to ויקרא 24:11. There, ויקב is followed by ויקלל, so the פסוק itself explains נוקב as cursing. This closes the question from step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you wish, say (an alternative answer)
and he blasphemed (here proven to mean cursed)

steps.whatToRemember: נוקב means cursing. We know it from בלעם's אקב, or from ויקב next to ויקלל. Piercing and pronouncing the name were both rejected.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
the verse says: "And he blasphemed... and cursed,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:11.

phrases.english: which shows that נוקב means cursing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative answer to the question in step 8, after the rival readings were rejected.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 24:11, where ויקב appears next to ויקלל.

steps.title: Maybe a person must do both acts to be liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof from step 18. Maybe 'ויקב' and 'ויקלל' are two separate acts, and a person is only liable once he does both.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe a person is not liable until he does both of them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof that נוקב means cursing. Maybe the פסוק lists two acts because both are needed for liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18 the גמרא said that because the פסוק says 'ויקב' and then 'ויקלל', the two words mean the same thing. Now it suggests another reading: they are two different acts, and the death penalty needs both. If so, we cannot prove that נוקב by itself means cursing.

phrases.english: But maybe [he is not liable] until he does both of them?
phrases.notes: 'Both' means both נוקב and cursing, the two words from the פסוק in step 18.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof that 'ויקב' and 'ויקלל' describe one act.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two words in a row could mean two needed acts, not one act said twice.

steps.title: The Torah calls him only 'the one who cursed', so it is one act
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge. When the Torah orders his punishment it says 'Bring out the one who cursed', not 'the נוקב and the one who cursed'. So the two words describe one act.
steps.simpleTranslation: That cannot be, because it says 'Bring out the one who cursed', and it does not say 'Bring out the נוקב and the one who cursed'. Learn from this that it is one act.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 19 and proves that נוקב and cursing are the same act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two separate acts were needed, the punishment פסוק should name both. Since it names only 'המקלל', the Torah treats the whole act as cursing. So the proof from step 18 stands: נוקב means cursing.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not even think that (a strong rejection)

steps.whatToRemember: נוקב in the פסוק (ונוקב שם ה׳ מות יומת) means cursing ה׳'s name. The Torah treats 'ויקב' and 'ויקלל' as one act, since the punishment פסוק names only 'המקלל'.

phrases.english: This should not enter your mind,
as it is written: "Bring out the one who cursed,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:14

phrases.english: and it is not written: "Bring out the נוקב and the one who cursed."
Learn from this that it is one [act].

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ, דִּכְתִיב: ״הוֹצֵא אֶת הַמְקַלֵּל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19 and confirms the proof of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from how the punishment פסוק is worded
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נוקב and cursing might be two acts that are both needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The punishment פסוק names only the מקלל, so נוקב and cursing are one act.

steps.title: Non-Jews are also forbidden to curse ה׳
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the double phrase 'איש איש' that non-Jews are also warned not to curse ה׳. Their punishment is death by the sword, like every death penalty for בני נח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: The פסוק could have said 'איש'. Why does it say 'איש איש'? To include non-Jews, who are warned against cursing ה׳ just like Jews. They are killed only by the sword, because every death penalty said about בני נח is only by the sword.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא. It teaches that the ban on cursing ה׳ applies to non-Jews too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'איש' widens the law beyond Jews to all people. The ברייתא also sets the punishment: a non-Jew is not stoned like a Jew, but killed by the sword, because that is the only death penalty for בני נח.

keyTerms.meaning: Any man; the doubled word adds something
Literally 'blessing the Name', a polite way to say cursing ה׳

steps.confusionAlert: 'בִּרְכַּת הַשֵּׁם' does not mean blessing ה׳. It is a polite way of saying cursing, so the words of the curse are not said out loud.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
[The פסוק could say] "a man". Why does the פסוק say "any man"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:15

phrases.english: To include the non-Jews,
who are warned against 'blessing' ה׳'s name, just like Jews are.
phrases.notes: 'Blessing' here is a polite way of saying cursing.

phrases.english: And they are killed only by the sword,
because every death penalty said about the descendants of נח
is only by the sword.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״אִישׁ״ – מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: whether cursing ה׳ applies to non-Jews.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Non-Jews are forbidden to curse ה׳, learned from 'איש איש', and are killed by the sword.
steps.whyThisMatters: This connects our sugya to the larger discussion of the מצוות of בני נח, which the גמרא develops next.

steps.title: We already know this from a different פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we need 'איש איש' for this law. We already learn that non-Jews may not curse ה׳ from a different source, where the word 'ה׳' teaches the ban on cursing the Name.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is this learned from here? It is learned from there: 'ה׳' refers to cursing the Name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. It points out that the ban on non-Jews cursing ה׳ already comes from another source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Another ברייתא learns the מצוות of בני נח from the פסוק said to אדם הראשון, and the word 'ה׳' there teaches the ban on cursing the Name. Since that already covers all people, the extra 'איש' seems unneeded for this.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it learned from here?
It is learned from there (a different source)

phrases.english: But is this learned from here?
It is learned from there:
"ה׳": this is [the ban on] cursing the Name.
phrases.notes: This is from the פסוק said to אדם הראשון, בראשית 2:16, which the גמרא will quote in full soon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source used in the ברייתא of step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of 'איש איש' to teach that non-Jews may not curse ה׳.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If another פסוק already teaches this law, the extra word 'איש' is not needed for it.

steps.title: The extra word includes cursing with a substitute name
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא answers that 'איש איש' is needed for something new: a non-Jew is also liable for cursing with a כינוי, a substitute name of ה׳, according to רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק נפחא said: It is needed only to include the substitute names, and this follows רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק נפחא answers the challenge by giving the extra word a new job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic ban comes from the פסוק to אדם הראשון. 'איש איש' adds that a non-Jew is also liable for cursing with a כינוי, not only with the real Name. This fits רבי מאיר, who gives the death penalty even for cursing with a כינוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Substitute names or titles of ה׳

steps.whatToRemember: The basic ban on non-Jews cursing ה׳ comes from the פסוק to אדם הראשון. 'איש איש' adds cursing with a כינוי, according to רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: רבי יצחק נפחא said:
It is needed only
to include the substitute names,
and this follows the view of רבי מאיר.
phrases.notes: רבי מאיר holds that cursing with a substitute name carries the death penalty, just like cursing the real Name.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַכִּינּוּיִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22 by giving the extra word a new teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra word a different job
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'איש איש' seemed to repeat a law already learned from the פסוק to אדם הראשון.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'איש איש' teaches that a non-Jew is also liable for cursing with a כינוי, according to רבי מאיר.

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי מאיר includes all substitute names
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks why the פסוק 'איש איש כי יקלל אלהיו' is needed, since the death penalty is already written in 'ונקב שם ה׳'. It answers that this פסוק teaches that cursing any כינוי is included. This is the view of רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: Why does the Torah write 'Anyone who curses his God shall bear his sin'? It already said 'One who curses the name of ה׳ shall be put to death'! Because it said 'the name', I might think a person is liable only for the שם המיוחד. How do we know that all the substitute names are included? The פסוק says 'Anyone who curses his God', meaning in every case. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for what רבי יצחק נפחא said in step 23. The ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר holds that cursing ה׳ with a כינוי is also a capital sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sees two פסוקים about cursing ה׳ and asks why we need both. Its answer: 'ונקב שם' alone would limit the death penalty to the שם המיוחד. The words 'יקלל אלהיו' add every כינוי. This is why רבי יצחק נפחא could say that, according to רבי מאיר, a כינוי counts.

keyTerms.meaning: The special, unique Name of ה׳ (the four-letter Name)
Substitute names or titles of ה׳
Why did the פסוק need to say this?
In every case, with no limit

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two פסוקים. 'ונקב שם' points to the special Name. 'יקלל אלהיו' is the wider phrase that brings in the כינויים according to רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: As it is taught: "Anyone who curses his God
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:15

phrases.english: shall bear his sin" — why does the verse need to say this?
Isn't it already stated:
"And one who curses the name of ה׳ shall be put to death"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:16

phrases.english: Since it says "one who curses the name shall be put to death,"
I might think he is not liable
except for the special Name alone.
From where do we include all the substitute names?

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אִישׁ כִּי יְקַלֵּל אֱלֹהָיו״ – מִכׇּל מָקוֹם.
phrases.english: The verse says: "Anyone who curses his God", meaning in any case.
These are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי יצחק נפחא's claim that רבי מאיר holds a כינוי is enough
steps.raayaObject: רבי יצחק נפחא's statement that, according to רבי מאיר, cursing with a כינוי is a liable act
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא reading 'יקלל אלהיו' as including all כינויים, according to רבי מאיר

steps.title: The חכמים: death only for the special Name
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר. Cursing the שם המיוחד carries death, but cursing a כינוי is only a plain prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: for the special Name the punishment is death, and for the substitute names it is only a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the חכמים, who argue with רבי מאיר. For them, the death penalty applies only to the שם המיוחד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that cursing a כינוי is forbidden. They argue only about the punishment. רבי מאיר gives death, while the חכמים treat it as a regular לאו without death.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Sages say (the majority view)
A warning, meaning a prohibition without the death penalty

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
for the special Name, it is punished by death,
and for the substitute names, it is only a prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view within the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, only the שם המיוחד brings death. A כינוי is a plain prohibition.

steps.title: רבי מיישא: a non-Jew is liable for a substitute name even according to the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יצחק נפחא argues with רבי מיישא. רבי מיישא holds that a בן נח who curses ה׳ with a כינוי is liable even according to the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with רבי מיישא, for רבי מיישא said: a בן נח who 'blessed' (meaning cursed) ה׳ with a substitute name is liable, even according to the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a different אמורא, רבי מיישא, disagrees with רבי יצחק נפחא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק נפחא tied the non-Jew's liability for a כינוי only to רבי מאיר. רבי מיישא says even the חכמים, who are lenient with a Jew, would hold a בן נח liable for a כינוי.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew, a descendant of נח
Who 'blessed' ה׳, a polite way of saying 'cursed'

steps.confusionAlert: 'בירך' here does not mean blessing. The גמרא avoids writing 'cursed ה׳' outright and uses the opposite word.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with רבי מיישא,
phrases.notes: He means: רבי יצחק נפחא's answer from step 23 does not fit רבי מיישא's view.

phrases.english: for רבי מיישא said:

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן נֹחַ שֶׁבֵּירַךְ אֶת הַשֵּׁם בְּכִינּוּי,
phrases.english: a descendant of נח who 'blessed' ה׳ with a substitute name,
even according to the Rabbis, is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows an אמורא who disagrees with רבי יצחק נפחא's answer
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בן נח is liable for cursing ה׳ with a כינוי, even according to the חכמים.

steps.title: What is רבי מיישא's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the חכמים would be stricter with a non-Jew than with a Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי מיישא's ruling. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It seems strange that a non-Jew would be liable for something a Jew is not put to death for. So the גמרא needs a source.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of רבי מיישא's ruling
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that the חכמים hold a בן נח liable for a כינוי

steps.title: The 'Name' condition is only for a convert and a born Jew
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'כגר כאזרח בנקבו שם' limits the need for the real Name to a גר and a born Jew. A non-Jew is liable even for a כינוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the פסוק says: 'the convert as well as the citizen'. It is only for a גר and a born Jew that we need 'when he curses the Name'. But a non-Jew is liable even with a substitute name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי מיישא's reason from the wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'כגר כאזרח' come right before 'בנקבו שם'. So the condition of the real Name is said only about Jews and converts. A non-Jew is left outside that limit, so for him even a כינוי brings liability.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: a כינוי brings death for anyone. The חכמים: for a Jew, only the שם המיוחד brings death. רבי יצחק נפחא says a non-Jew is liable for a כינוי only according to רבי מאיר. רבי מיישא says a non-Jew is liable for a כינוי even according to the חכמים, because 'בנקבו שם' was said only about a גר and a born Jew.

phrases.english: Because the verse says: "The convert as well as the citizen".
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:16

phrases.english: It is a convert and a citizen
for whom we require "when he curses the Name",
but a non-Jew is liable even with a substitute name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כגר כאזרח' limits the 'שם' requirement to Jews and converts, so a non-Jew is liable even for a כינוי.

steps.title: What does רבי מאיר learn from 'כגר כאזרח'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי מאיר does with the words 'כגר כאזרח'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר, what does he do with the words 'the convert as well as the homeborn'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי מאיר learns from the words 'כגר כאזרח'. He makes anyone who curses with a כינוי liable, so he cannot use these words the way the חכמים did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 28 the חכמים used 'כגר כאזרח' to teach that only a Jew needs the real Name. רבי מאיר holds that even a Jew is liable for a כינוי, so he doesn't need that lesson. The גמרא now asks what these words teach in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? (What does he learn from this פסוק?)
The convert as well as the homeborn (ויקרא 24:16)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir,
this phrase 'the convert as well as the homeborn',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:16

phrases.english: what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, הַאי ״כַּגֵּר כָּאֶזְרָח״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 28 used the פסוק for the חכמים. Now the גמרא asks how רבי מאיר uses it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson רבי מאיר learns from 'כגר כאזרח', since he doesn't need it to limit the need for the real Name.

steps.title: A Jew gets סקילה, a non-Jew gets סייף
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר learns that a גר or born Jew is killed by סקילה, but a non-Jew by סייף. Without the פסוק, we might think the non-Jew also gets סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A convert or a born Jew is killed by stoning, but a non-Jew is killed by the sword. You might have thought that since non-Jews were included in this law, they are included in everything, so the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for רבי מאיר, 'כגר כאזרח' teaches the type of death. A Jew who curses ה׳ gets סקילה, but a non-Jew gets סייף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since non-Jews are included in the sin of cursing ה׳, we might have thought they share the same punishment too. The פסוק limits סקילה to a גר and a born Jew. A non-Jew gets the usual death of a בן נח, which is סייף.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought to say...

phrases.english: A convert or a born Jew is killed by stoning,
but a non-Jew is killed by the sword.
It might enter your mind to say:
since they were included, they are fully included –
phrases.notes: He means that since non-Jews are included in the sin of cursing ה׳, you might think they also get the same punishment.

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: גֵּר וְאֶזְרָח בִּסְקִילָה, אֲבָל גּוֹי בְּסַיִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי מאיר, 'כגר כאזרח' limits סקילה to Jews. A non-Jew who curses ה׳ is killed by סייף.

steps.title: What does רבי יצחק נפחא learn from 'כגר כאזרח'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יצחק נפחא, explaining the חכמים, uses the words 'כגר כאזרח'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק נפחא, according to the חכמים, what does he do with the words 'the convert as well as the homeborn'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question for רבי יצחק נפחא. He explains the חכמים in a way that argues with רבי מיישא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 26 we learned that רבי יצחק נפחא argues with רבי מיישא. He does not hold that the חכמים make a non-Jew liable for a כינוי. So he cannot use 'כגר כאזרח' the way step 28 did, and the גמרא asks what he learns from it.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of the חכמים

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha, according to the Rabbis,
this phrase 'the convert as well as the homeborn',
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא, אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּנַן, הַאי ״כַּגֵּר כָּאֶזְרָח״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the same question as step 29, now for the other opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson רבי יצחק נפחא, explaining the חכמים, learns from 'כגר כאזרח'.

steps.title: Only a Jew needs to curse 'שם בשם'
steps.stepSummary: A Jew is liable only if he curses the Name of ה׳ by the Name of ה׳. A non-Jew is liable even without that.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a convert and a born Jew who need to curse 'a Name by a Name'. A non-Jew does not need 'a Name by a Name'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יצחק נפחא learns a different limit from 'כגר כאזרח'. Only a Jew must curse the Name using the Name (שם בשם) to be liable. A non-Jew is liable even without this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the limit is not about כינויים. It is about the form of the curse. For a Jew, the curse must use ה׳'s Name against ה׳'s Name. For a non-Jew, this extra requirement does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: A Name by a Name: cursing ה׳'s Name using ה׳'s Name

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 28. There the limit was about the real Name versus a כינוי. Here it is about whether the curse must be 'שם בשם'.

phrases.english: It is a convert and a born Jew for whom we require
a Name by a Name,
phrases.notes: This means the curse uses ה׳'s Name against ה׳'s Name.

phrases.english: but for a non-Jew we do not require
a Name by a Name.

steps.triggerLanguage: גֵּר וְאֶזְרָח הוּא דְּבָעֵינַן שֵׁם בְּשֵׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כגר כאזרח' teaches that only a Jew needs 'שם בשם' to be liable. A non-Jew does not.

steps.title: Why does the תורה say 'איש איש'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the Torah doubles the word 'איש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Anyone, anyone', why do I need it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the פסוק says 'איש איש', with the word written twice. The חכמים do not learn כינויים from it, so what is the extra word for?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 24, רבי מאיר used 'איש איש כי יקלל אלהיו' to include כינויים. The חכמים disagree with that lesson, so the doubled word seems extra in their view.

phrases.english: 'Anyone, anyone' – why do I need it?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:15. This is asked for the views that don't use these words to include כינויים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining 'כגר כאזרח', the גמרא now explains the other part of the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the doubled word 'איש איש' teaches for those who don't learn כינויים from it.

steps.title: The תורה speaks like people do
steps.stepSummary: The doubled word teaches nothing new. The Torah used normal human speech.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah spoke in the language of people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'איש איש' is not meant to teach anything extra. People often double words when they talk, and the Torah does the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a known approach to reading the Torah. Not every repeated word teaches a new law; sometimes it is just normal style. This ends the discussion of the cursing פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah spoke in the language of people

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: a כינוי counts for everyone. A Jew gets סקילה and a non-Jew gets סייף. חכמים: a Jew needs the real Name. A non-Jew is liable even for a כינוי according to רבי מיישא, and without 'שם בשם' according to רבי יצחק נפחא. 'איש איש' is normal human speech.

phrases.english: The Torah spoke in the language of people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The doubled 'איש איש' is ordinary human speech and teaches no new law.

steps.title: The seven מצוות of בני נח
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists the seven מצוות that all בני נח were commanded.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: בני נח were commanded seven מצוות: setting up courts, not cursing ה׳, not worshipping idols, not doing forbidden relations, not killing, not stealing, and not eating a limb from a living animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that starts a new section. It lists the seven מצוות that apply to all people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion of a בן נח cursing ה׳ leads to a full discussion of all seven מצוות בני נח. This list is the base text. The coming steps will discuss where each מצוה comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: The seven מצוות commanded to all people
'Blessing' ה׳'s Name, a polite way of saying cursing ה׳
A limb cut from a living animal

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the main source for the seven מצוות בני נח, the laws the Torah expects of all mankind.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The descendants of Noach were commanded seven מצוות –
courts of justice, and cursing the Name,
idol worship, forbidden relations,
and murder, and robbery,
and a limb from a living animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שֶׁבַע מִצְוֹת נִצְטַוּוּ בְּנֵי נֹחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the one law of a בן נח cursing ה׳ to the full list of מצוות בני נח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All people are commanded seven מצוות: דינין, ברכת השם, עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות, שפיכות דמים, גזל, and אבר מן החי.
